title: Entryway Organization for Coat and Boot Season (Wet Mittens Included)
description: Keep coats, boots, hats and wet mittens from taking over the front door this winter. Easy ADHD-friendly entryway ideas plus 8 Amazon finds.
intro:
Summer entryway: a pair of sandals and a tote bag. Winter entryway: four puffy coats, nine boots, a sad pile of wet mittens and one glove that belongs to nobody.

Colder weather doubles the amount of stuff that comes through the front door, and it's all bulky, damp and needed again tomorrow morning. If the entryway doesn't have a spot for it, it lands on the floor, the stairs or the kitchen chair.

Here's how to set up the door for coat and boot season, plus eight Amazon finds that make it easy to keep up with.

sections.heading: Think 'drop zone,' not 'closet'
sections.body:
Coat closets are great for coats you wear twice a month. For the ones you wear every day, a closet door is one step too many. Our brains are drawn to the nearest flat surface, so we need the storage to be *right there* and *open*.

The goal: everything you take off at the door has a spot within arm's reach of where you're standing when you take it off.

sections.heading: Hooks beat hangers, every time
sections.body:
A hanger takes two hands and a decision. A hook takes one hand and zero thought. Put up a row of sturdy hooks at adult height and a second, lower row for kids.

Give each person their own hook (or two). Label them if it helps. When everyone has a spot, it's easier to see whose coat is on the floor.

sections.heading: Boots need a tray
sections.body:
Wet boots on bare floors mean puddles, salt stains and slipping. A boot tray with a lip catches the mess and gives boots one obvious place to live.

Put it right inside the door so boots come off on the tray, not three steps into the house. If space is tight, a tall, narrow boot rack holds more pairs in less floor.

sections.heading: One basket per person for hats and gloves
sections.body:
Hats, gloves and scarves are small, which means they disappear. Give each person one basket or bin on a shelf or bench. No sorting by type. Everything that person wears on their head and hands goes in their basket.

Mornings get easier when "where's my other glove?" has one place to check.

sections.heading: Set up a drying spot
sections.body:
Wet mittens tossed in a basket stay wet (and get a smell). Add a small drying rack, a few clips on a hook or a mesh hanging bag near a heat vent so damp stuff dries overnight.

It doesn't need to be pretty. It needs to be close enough that you actually use it.

sections.heading: Do a two-minute Sunday sweep
sections.body: Once a week, take two minutes at the door: send stray shoes back to bedrooms, toss any trash out of the bench, and match up the gloves. Set a timer and stop when it rings. Small and regular beats big and never.

outro:
Winter brings a lot of stuff through the door. Give every coat, boot and mitten a spot within arm's reach and the pile stops building itself.

Want help with the rest of the house too? *The Messy Brain Home Reset* walks you through one small zone at a time, the entryway included.
